inputs.share_count_basis: 2,031.09m ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY26 AR note 10(a)) + ~2.0m dilutive performance rights (diluted vs basic weighted average, note 4) + ~15.6m scrip shares for the Carnaby Resources scheme (~A$213m at ~A$13.65; completion expected late Oct/early Nov 2026, matched by a A$213m equity-bridge item at cost). Held FLAT thereafter: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and the DRP (17.2m shares / A$152.5m in FY26) is dividend reinvestment, i.e. cash retained rather than a cost, so it is neither a dilution charge nor an issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR consolidated statement of comprehensive income, 'Share-based payments expense' 37,329 ($'000); equity-award taxes disclosed as nil (net-share settlement not used). Interest income 34,614 stripped because the A$1,347.5m cash pile sits in the bridge.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built, single rate for all scenarios: AUD 10y government ~4.4% + beta ~0.85 x ERP 5.5% = ~9.1% cost of equity; pre-tax debt cost 4.47% (fixed-rate USPP, swapped) = ~3.1% after tax; debt ~5% of capital at market -> WACC ~8.8%, rounded to 9.0%. Gold-price cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows (mid-cycle reversion in base, A$4,300/oz in bear), not as a WACC premium, and no per-scenario WACC difference: risk charged once.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt: A$35.8m of lease liabilities (15.5 current + 20.3 non-current) are inside total_debt/net_debt; no lease principal is deducted from the flows; the ~A$52m/yr of fleet-lease renewal (FY26 principal payments 52,282) is folded into capex_pct (+~1pp) and right-of-use depreciation (~A$50m) stays inside da_pct, so lease cash is charged exactly once.
inputs.nci_treatment: None required. FY26 profit (A$1,475.1m) and total equity (A$5,828.8m) are 100% attributable to Evolution shareholders; the 80% Northparkes interest is an unincorporated JV proportionately consolidated, so there is no NCI line in the statements.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF with MID-CYCLE commodity treatment (SKILL.md row 'operating company, cyclical' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). FY26 is a peak-cycle year: achieved gold A$6,023/oz (+40% YoY, +154% over five years) against AISC A$1,717/oz, EBITDA margin 54.8% vs 44.4% in FY24 and 38% in FY23; the company is now fully unhedged. The base case therefore does NOT extrapolate FY26: gold is reverted from spot ~A$6,140/oz (US$4,370 / AUDUSD 0.7119 on 2026-09-22) to ~A$5,300/oz by FY29 (roughly 14% below spot, still ~18% above the FY24-26 achieved average of A$4,504), with FY27 production at guidance midpoint (695koz gold, 66.5kt copper) and cash costs escalating 3%/yr on top of the guided FY27 step-up (AISC A$1,795-1,995/oz). Capex follows FY27 guidance (~A$1.5bn: sustaining 265-325 + mine development 440-500 + major project 570-650 + exploration 130-160) through the E22 block cave / OPC / Bert build, then normalises to D&A (~18% of revenue) by FY32 -- the classic reserve-replacement steady state for a miner. Cash tax ramps 28% -> 31% (FY26 cash tax was only 18.7% of PBT on timing and accelerated mining deductions; effective rate 32.6%). Terminal value capped at 14x owner FCF (cyclical range 12-15x, upper half because copper by-product credits and Tier-1 asset lives make EVN a lower-cost, longer-duration producer than pure-gold peers); Gordon at 9%/2.5% would be 15.8x, so the cap binds in every scenario. Historical CAGRs (revenue 24% 5yr, owner FCF 35% 5yr) describe the gold up-cycle, not growth capacity, and are not used as a growth basis. Data note: the Metrics CSV 'Depreciation' KPI (858.2) differs from the FY26 income-statement D&A of 755.5 (note 2); the model anchors da_pct on the 755.5 statement figure plus ROU depreciation. Triple Flag stream deferred revenue (A$578m) is left as an operating item because the below-market delivery pricing is already inside FY26 revenue; it is a debt-like obligation a stricter bridge could deduct (~A$0.28/share).

equity_bridge.item: Carnaby Resources (Greater Duchess copper-gold) at scrip cost
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR note 19(b): ~A$213m scheme consideration in EVN shares, matched by the ~15.6m shares added to shares_outstanding; asset carried at cost so the deal is value-neutral by construction, with the ~10ktpa copper option treated as bull-case upside.

equity_bridge.item: Equity investments at fair value + equity-accounted investments
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR balance sheet: 55.03 (FVOCI listed equities incl. the Arizona Gold & Silver stake) + 7.19 (equity accounted); their income is not in the flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment: terminal nominal drift (volume +2-3%/yr FY29-31 from Bert/E22/OPC offset by gold-price reversion); not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 18.1% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 29.2% (38% divergence) and revenue 24.4%. All CAGRs are driven by the achieved gold price rising from A$2,369/oz (FY21) to A$6,023/oz (FY26) on flat-to-lower production (681koz -> 715koz); they measure the commodity cycle, not the company's growth capacity, and are not used as a growth input.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR is undefined because FY23 owner FCF was negative (reported -103.4 - SBC 12.9 - interest 8.0 = -124.3) during the Cowal underground / Red Lake build. Owner-FCF series: FY21 306.5, FY22 92.9, FY23 -124.3, FY24 345.5, FY25 750.8, FY26 1,360.2 (reported FCF less SBC less interest income). Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (34.7%) is slightly below reported (35.0%): SBC has grown from 0.6% to 0.67% of revenue, immaterial.

base.growth_note: FY27: production at guidance midpoint (695koz gold -3%, 66.5kt copper flat) at spot ~A$6,140/oz -> revenue ~A$5.53bn. FY28-29: gold reverts to A$5,700 then A$5,300/oz while volumes rise ~3%/yr (Bert first ore FY29, Cowal OPC). FY30-31: +5%/+4% as Northparkes E22/CPF ramps (copper) with 2% nominal price drift. FY32+: 2.5% nominal.
base.margin_note: FY27 55% = FY27 guidance cash costs ~A$2.44bn (AISC midpoint A$1,895/oz x 695koz + by-product credits - sustaining capex + corporate/exploration expensed; Mt Rawdon closure and no repeat of the A$45m Ernest Henry flood cost) on ~A$5.53bn revenue; costs then escalate 3%/yr plus volume, royalties fall with price, giving 48% at A$5,300/oz gold and a slow drift to 46% as cost inflation outruns nominal price drift. Comparable actuals: FY24 44.4% at A$3,190/oz, FY25 49.7% at A$4,300/oz, FY26 54.8% at A$6,023/oz.
base.capex_note: FY27 28% = ~A$1.5bn guided cash capex (sustaining ~295 + mine development ~470 + major projects ~610 + capitalised exploration ~130) plus ~A$52m lease renewal; FY28 peak of the E22 block cave; then normalising to D&A (18%) by FY32 once E22, OPC and Bert are in production.
base.tax_note: Cash tax 28% -> 31%: FY26 cash tax A$408.6m was 18.7% of PBT (current tax liability up A$83m, deferred tax liability up A$152m on accelerated mining deductions); effective rate 32.6% (Australia 30% + Canadian mining tax). Ramps as capex normalises.

bull.growth_note: Gold holds A$6,300/oz in FY27 and A$6,500/oz in FY28 (US$4,600 at 0.71 -- still below the US$4,900-6,300 bank forecasts), drifting +2%/yr nominal thereafter; production ramps to ~800koz gold and ~90kt copper by FY31 as Bert, OPC, E22/CPF and Carnaby's Greater Duchess deliver on schedule; copper +5-10%/yr FY29-31.
bull.margin_note: Margins hold at ~56-57% (FY26 underlying EBITDA margin was 57.1%) because price drift matches cost escalation and by-product credits grow with copper volumes.

bear.growth_note: Gold corrects to A$5,600/oz in FY27, A$4,800 in FY28 and A$4,300/oz by FY29 (~US$3,050 -- the FY25 achieved level and the FY24-26 average) with copper -10%; volumes at the bottom of guidance then +1.5-2%/yr as growth projects are slowed; 2% nominal thereafter.
bear.margin_note: Margins compress to 36-39% (between FY23's 38% at A$2,592/oz and FY24's 44% at A$3,190/oz, adjusted for three years of cost escalation) because the unhedged book gives no protection and only royalties flex with price. D&A stays high on the historical cost base as volumes and capex are cut, so terminal capex (19%) sits just below D&A (20%).

scenario_narratives.base: The axes for Evolution are (1) where the gold price settles after a three-year run from A$2,400 to A$6,000+/oz, now fully unhedged, (2) whether the copper by-product engine (Ernest Henry, Northparkes E22/CPF, Carnaby) offsets the structural AISC climb from A$907 to ~A$1,900/oz, and (3) whether the ~A$1.5bn/yr capital programme delivers its projects on budget and then rolls off. Base: production meets FY27 guidance (695koz, 66.5kt) at spot, gold then reverts to ~A$5,300/oz by FY29 -- 14% below spot, well above the five-year average -- while Bert, OPC and E22 lift volumes ~3%/yr from FY29. EBITDA margin falls from 55% to ~47% as 3%/yr cost escalation outruns nominal price drift; capex peaks at ~29% of revenue in FY28 and normalises to D&A (~18%) by FY32; cash tax ramps to 31%. Terminal value is capped at 14x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Gold holds A$6,300-6,500/oz (below the US$4,900-6,300 bank forecasts) and drifts with inflation; the growth pipeline delivers on schedule, taking production to ~800koz gold and ~90kt copper by FY31 with Carnaby's Greater Duchess adding ~10ktpa copper through Ernest Henry's mill. Margins hold at the FY26 underlying level (~56%) because growing by-product credits absorb cost inflation; capex rolls off to 16.5% of revenue as the E22 build completes; revenue compounds ~5%/yr through FY31 and 3.5% thereafter.
scenario_narratives.bear: A hawkish Fed surprise, dollar strength or the slowdown in central-bank buying already visible in Q1 2026 (16t vs the ~225t/quarter 2021-25 average) takes gold back to ~A$4,300/oz by FY29 -- the FY25 achieved price -- with copper 10% lower. The unhedged book offers no cushion, AISC keeps escalating on labour, fuel and royalties, and legacy-asset declines (Cowal, Ernest Henry, Northparkes, Mt Rawdon closed) hold volumes at the bottom of guidance while E22/Bert are slowed. Revenue falls ~23% over three years, EBITDA margin compresses to ~36-39%, and the FY27-28 committed capex is spent into a falling price, leaving owner FCF near zero for two years before recovering to ~A$450-500m/yr.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the entire earnings step-up is a commodity price that has tripled in three years, the company has just removed its last hedges, central-bank demand has visibly slowed, and the FY27-28 capital programme is committed regardless of price. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs gold to hold at or above a record nominal price AND four concurrent projects (OPC, E22/CPF, Bert, Carnaby) to deliver on schedule -- several independent things. Base 50%: guidance-anchored FY27 with a mid-cycle reversion that still sits ~18% above the FY24-26 average achieved price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Evolution as a long-life, copper-credited gold producer on mid-cycle cash flows rather than on FY26's record. Owner FCF is reported FCF less SBC and interest income; the forward build starts from FY27 guidance (production, AISC, ~A$1.5bn capex) at spot gold and then reverts price toward a mid-cycle level while volumes grow from the funded pipeline. Cyclicality is charged once, in the scenario flows and their weights, at a single AUD WACC of 9%; the terminal multiple is capped at 14x owner FCF because a buyer of a gold miner at the top of the cycle is not granted a Gordon multiple. The house value is what the assets earn through a cycle; the gap to the market price measures how much of spot gold, capitalised at a sub-8% rate, the market is paying for.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gold price: every A$500/oz on ~700koz is ~A$350m of EBITDA (~6pp of margin); the base assumes A$5,300/oz mid-cycle, the market implies spot or higher in perpetuity
Fully unhedged since the final FY26 hedge delivery: no downside protection on the price reversion the bear case models
Capex step-up: FY27 guidance ~A$1.5bn (28% of revenue) into E22 block cave, OPC, Bert and Mungari; overruns or delays defer the FY30-31 volume growth the base and bull cases rely on
AISC escalation: A$907/oz (FY16) to A$1,717/oz (FY26) and guided A$1,795-1,995/oz for FY27 -- labour is ~half the cost base and royalties are price-linked
Cash tax normalisation: FY26 paid only 18.7% of PBT; a catch-up on the A$288.6m current tax liability plus a 31% run-rate removes ~A$250m/yr of the FY26 FCF base
Operational hazards: the Dec-2025/Mar-2026 Ernest Henry flooding cost ~12koz gold, ~8kt copper and A$45m; Mt Rawdon processing ceases in the Sep-2026 quarter
Triple Flag stream (A$578m deferred revenue) is a debt-like obligation left inside the operating flows; a stricter bridge deducts ~A$0.28/share
Carnaby completion (ACCC, scheme vote late Oct/early Nov 2026): modelled as value-neutral at A$213m scrip; the copper option is bull-case only
